our_view.thesis_status: This is the cleanest and best-performing credit onboarded in this batch so far: 18 straight months of certified TTM FCCR (2025-01 through 2026-06), rising MONOTONICALLY every single month from 1.6680x to 2.1564x against a flat 1.2000x minimum -- covenant cushion has nearly tripled (0.47x to 0.96x headroom). All four quarterly tests to date (2025-Q1, Q2, Q3, Q4, plus 2026-Q1, Q2 -- six consecutive quarter-end tests) certified COMPLIANT with growing margin, and TTM Covenant EBITDA has grown every quarter checked ($23.3M at 2025-01 to $29.2M at 2026-06). There is no amendment or waiver chain (none exists), no restatement or correction notice anywhere in the 22-month reporting history, and every monthly package file-shape check (spot-checked across 6 months spanning the full range) came back byte-consistent with no deviations. The credit thesis pillars are all intact and, if anything, understated at underwriting -- the deal was sized around a 1.3016x stressed-downside FCCR floor, and actual performance has moved to nearly double that even in the base case. The two genuine flags worth carrying forward are structural, not performance-related: (1) the collateral package is a specific-asset lien (receivables + equipment + IP), materially narrower than a blanket lien, leaving inventory and other current assets outside the lender's security; and (2) the facility's 0.20%/month amortization leaves a large balloon due at the January 2030 maturity that depends on continued refinancing capacity -- not an imminent concern given the current trend, but the IC Memo names it explicitly as a structural risk.
our_view.what_would_change_our_mind: Watchlist would move toward 'on'/trajectory toward 'stable' or 'deteriorating' if: (a) the FCCR trend flattens or reverses at the next quarterly test (2026-Q3, September 30, 2026); (b) any restatement, correction notice, or file-shape deviation appears in future monthly packages, given how clean the record has been to date; (c) evidence emerges that the Working DRAFT department mapping (which swaps two Sales accounts' GL categories) was ever used in place of the Approved mapping for any actual budget or monitoring output; or (d) any named customer/vendor concentration data becomes available and reveals a concentration risk not currently visible in the bucketed-totals-only aging file.

covenants.agreement_ref: Talvorn 2025 Senior Secured Credit Facility -- Executed Credit Agreement between Talvorn Technical Services, LLC (Borrower) and Blue Mesa Private Credit, LP (Administrative Agent). Issued January 10, 2025; effective January 15, 2025; maturity January 15, 2030. Par refinancing of $104,139,422.73 of legacy (January 2022) principal; no new money, no sponsor equity, single obligor (no guarantors -- 'no unidentified subsidiary guarantor is certified' per the executed Guaranty and Security Agreement). No amendments or waivers exist in the deal folder: a full-text sweep of every executed document in Credit & Legal/Executed (original_agreement.pdf) and Credit & Legal/Executed/Initial Closing/ (fee-letter, guaranty-and-security, ip-security-agreement, funding-request, information-certificate, insurance-certificate, liquidity-certificate, officer-certificate, closing-compliance-certificate) for 'amend' and 'waiv' returns no hits describing a legal amendment or waiver of the credit agreement -- the only 'amend' hit anywhere in the Credit & Legal folder is the Board Finance Committee Mapping Policy's own express disclaimer that it 'does not amend the credit agreement.' No Amendments/ or Waivers/ subfolder exists anywhere in the deal folder structure.
transcription_notes: Transcribed the 'FCCR CALCULATION' section (Trailing Covenant EBITDA / Trailing Fixed Charges / Calculated FCCR / Minimum FCCR / Status) from SIX separate quarter-end compliance certificates, one per test date since the facility's first_test_date: certificate.pdf inside Finance Uploads/Monthly Close/2025/03, 2025/06, 2025/09, 2025/12, 2026/03 and 2026/06. Each is a distinct physical file that happens to share the identical filename 'certificate.pdf' across every month's folder (confirmed: 18 of 18 months 2025-01 through 2026-06 each carry their own certificate.pdf, per the execution config's own _compliance_certificate_folder_note). The 'value' transcribed per test date is the certificate's own 'Calculated FCCR' line -- a bare number stated by the borrower, not derived.

JUDGMENT CALL (recorded per the module's 'source' field, which is singular): this file's top-level 'source' is set to the bare filename 'certificate.pdf' per the module spec's documented shape, which lets the engine locate ONE representative file via its own recursive search of reporting_packages_folder (compliance_certificate_folder is blank for this borrower). Because every month's certificate shares that same filename, the engine's search resolves to whichever one instance it encounters first (folder-walk order, not necessarily 2026-06's own certificate) -- the source_files entry the engine attaches to these cert refs may therefore point at a DIFFERENT month's certificate.pdf than the one a given test-date value was actually read from. To keep every value independently traceable regardless of which file the engine's search resolves to, each value's own 'quote' field embeds that certificate's own header and 'Reporting period' line, naming its exact source certificate in the transcription itself. Alternative reading: run six separate certified-values files (one per historical period) through six separate engine invocations, each with its own period-matched 'source' -- rejected because the task calls for one consolidated cross-check across all reachable test dates in a single module output, and the per-entry quote already disambiguates the physical file.

The FCCR is tested QUARTERLY only -- interim (non-quarter-end) months in the borrower's monthly package also carry a running FCCR figure marked 'NOT TESTED' (informational only, per the execution config's own note) and are NOT transcribed here as certified test results, consistent with the covenant-spec's own note that only quarter-end dates are tested under a flat, non-stepped 1.20x minimum.

No amendments or waivers exist for this facility (confirmed by covenant-spec.json's own full-text sweep) and Covenant EBITDA is contractually defined to equal Reported EBITDA with zero permitted add-backs, so no add-back reconciliation was needed while transcribing these six certificates.

performance.methodology: Company-prepared/unaudited monthly financials model (read via monitor_lib). EBITDA is the model's single pinned bridge row. Normalized metrics strip config.comparability_items. Ratios are spot on latest-month flows; leverage/coverage are TTM within the current same-basis segment when >=12 such months exist. Standouts, drift, trend and the MoM bridge are objective/mechanical and confined to same-basis segments; the line read covers EVERY IS/BS leaf with rule-based flags (no statistical gating); narrative interpretation is left to synthesis.
